dataRefreshStatus.channel: Lee County Clerk of Court via FMB Chamber of Commerce
dataRefreshStatus.note: Publicly-published Lee County reports contain aggregate county totals only; Tourist Development Tax data is exempt from public records under Florida statute. FMB-specific figures require direct request through the appropriate channel.

dataRefreshStatus.metric: Residential housing — pre-Ian (2022) vs current FMB-specific baselines, SPLIT by property type (residential vs condo): active listings + annual closings + median price + DOM
dataRefreshStatus.channel: RPCRA (Royal Palm Coast Realtor Association) / Lee County Property Appraiser via FMB Chamber
dataRefreshStatus.note: The dashboard needs pre-Ian vs current FMB-specific comparisons split by property type (single-family residential and condo/timeshare track separately — condo recovery typically lags residential because of HOA dynamics, structural-reinforcement requirements, and association-level rebuild decisions). Required data: (1) active listings pre-Ian + current, by type; (2) annual sales volume 2022 full-year + trailing-12-month, by type; (3) median price + days on market 2022 vs current, by type if separable. Current dashboard shows only YoY direction (Feb 2026 +69%, Dec 2025 +68%) plus aggregate Feb 2026 median + DOM from Redfin.

capacityVsRevenue.interpretation: Capacity has rebuilt faster than per-unit revenue. Each rebuilt room is generating less revenue than its pre-Ian counterpart — lower occupancy, lower rates, or both. The directional finding (capacity ahead of revenue) is durable; the specific 18-point figure is a snapshot bounded by the dates of the two underlying numbers and will move as bed tax data refreshes.

sectors.title: Tourism & Lodging Capacity
sectors.lead: Lodging is FMB's economic engine. Pre-Ian, the town was Lee County's #1 bed-tax generator at $8.2M/year. Recovery here drives recovery everywhere else.

metrics.label: Hotel Rooms Operating
metrics.note: 1,306 hotel rooms operating across 20 properties (vs 1,724 pre-Ian). Includes the new 254-room Margaritaville Beach Resort which opened post-Ian. At surviving pre-Ian properties, ~93% of room capacity is back online (1,052 of 1,134 surviving pre-Ian rooms); the remaining 590 rooms are at 19 properties permanently lost.
metrics.source: Fort Myers Beach Chamber of Commerce, Accommodations file (March 18, 2026). Hotel data as of 7/30/2025.
metrics.trendLabel: Stronger than the Google-Places business database alone suggests

metrics.label: Hotel Properties Operating
metrics.note: 20 of 40 pre-Ian hotel properties are operating. 19 properties were permanently destroyed (590 rooms lost); 1 remains temporarily closed. Property-count recovery lags room-count recovery because surviving properties have larger room counts on average.
metrics.source: Fort Myers Beach Chamber of Commerce, Accommodations file (March 18, 2026).

metrics.label: Vacation Rental Rooms Operating
metrics.note: Three-bucket reconciliation of the 4,539 pre-Ian VR inventory: (1) 2,853 rooms currently operating; (2) 226 rooms permanently destroyed (6 VR properties: Bahama Beach Club, Palm Terrace, Royal Beach Club, Signature Vacation Rentals, Windward Passage time shares, Villa Del Mar); (3) the remaining 1,460-room gap is in rebuilding/partial-operation properties — 624 rooms across 12 explicitly-closed VR properties (per Chamber) plus ~836 rooms at properties operating with reduced inventory (e.g., Caribbean Beach Club currently 24/44; Cresciente 85/172; Coastal Breeze 38/125). VR Chamber-tracked inventory uses room counts; the FMB business database tracks licenses (1,982 active + 160 delinquent = 2,142) — different lens, see Watchlist.
metrics.source: Fort Myers Beach Chamber of Commerce, Accommodations file (March 18, 2026). VR numbers refreshed March 2026.
metrics.trendLabel: 63% of pre-Ian VR capacity operating; 226 rooms permanently lost

metrics.label: Delinquent VR Licenses (Likely Offline)
metrics.note: 160 vacation rental licenses are delinquent — properties unable to operate. 7.5% of 2,142 total licenses (1,982 active + 160 delinquent).
metrics.trendLabel: Leading indicator — these properties have not returned to operation

metrics.label: Tourist Attractions Operating
metrics.note: 32 of 33 tracked tourist attractions operational. 1 temporarily closed.

metrics.label: Bed Tax Recovery (YTD)
metrics.note: FMB collected $3.85M through August of FY25 — 48% of its $8.04M pre-Ian baseline. Curve: 15% → 37% → 48%. FMB share of Lee County total: 8.58% (was 12.49% pre-Ian, #1 municipal contributor).
metrics.source: Lee County Clerk of Court, Tourist Development Tax breakdown by municipality.

sectors.title: Watchlist — Leading Indicators
sectors.lead: Headline counts can mask trouble. These are the signals to watch quarter-over-quarter for early warning that recovery is stalling.

metrics.label: Café Closure Concentration
metrics.note: 3 of 7 cafés temporarily closed — 43% closure rate. Cafés have marginal economics and reopen last when foot traffic is slow to return. Highest closure rate of any category.
metrics.trendLabel: Concentrated risk — watch for further closures or reopenings

metrics.label: Currently Closed Businesses
metrics.note: 5 businesses temporarily closed: 3 cafés, 1 tourist attraction, 1 service business. 0 permanently closed (any business that fully closed would not appear in this dataset).
metrics.trendLabel: Small denominator — the 160 delinquent VR licenses are a larger risk signal

metrics.label: Population
metrics.note: 5,513 residents (2024 ACS estimate) vs 5,582 at 2020 Census. Surface number looks flat, but US Census Bureau ACS reports a -21.8% change 2019-2024, suggesting fluctuation around displacement and partial return.
metrics.source: US Census Bureau Quick Facts; American Community Survey 2024 estimates.
metrics.trendLabel: Population is context, not a recovery metric per se

housingMarket.headline: Pre-Ian vs current baselines pending — RPCRA data request in progress
housingMarket.framing: Housing recovery is shown here as pre-Ian (2022) vs current (2026), split by property type. Condo recovery typically lags single-family residential on barrier islands — HOA dynamics, structural-reinforcement requirements, and association-level rebuild decisions slow individual-unit return. FMB's heavy condo and timeshare inventory makes the split material. The four placeholder cards below show those comparisons (Residential vs Condo × Active Listings vs Annual Sales), pending RPCRA data via the FMB Chamber. The two cards beneath are the direction indicators and Redfin context we have today.

metrics.label: Residential — Active Listings (pre-Ian vs current)
metrics.note: Active single-family residential listings on Fort Myers Beach: pre-Ian (2022) baseline vs current (2026). Both pending RPCRA / Lee County Property Appraiser.
metrics.refreshStatus: Pre-Ian and current FMB-specific active-listing counts for single-family residential requested from RPCRA via FMB Chamber.

metrics.label: Residential — Annual Sales Volume (pre-Ian vs current)
metrics.note: Single-family residential closings on FMB: 2022 full-year (pre-Ian baseline) vs trailing-12-month (current). The transaction-volume side of residential recovery.
metrics.refreshStatus: 2022 monthly closings + trailing-12-month total for single-family residential requested from RPCRA via FMB Chamber.

metrics.label: Condo — Active Listings (pre-Ian vs current)
metrics.note: Active condo and timeshare listings on FMB: pre-Ian vs current. The condo story typically lags residential because HOA decisions, structural reinforcement, and association-level rebuild votes slow individual-unit return.
metrics.refreshStatus: Pre-Ian and current FMB-specific active-listing counts for condos and timeshares requested from RPCRA via FMB Chamber.

metrics.label: Condo — Annual Sales Volume (pre-Ian vs current)
metrics.note: Condo closings on FMB: 2022 full-year (pre-Ian) vs trailing-12-month (current). Condo sales typically recover more slowly than residential because of association-level constraints.
metrics.refreshStatus: 2022 monthly closings + trailing-12-month total for condo properties requested from RPCRA via FMB Chamber.

metrics.label: Home Sales — recent month (YoY direction)
metrics.confirmingDataPoint: December 2025 (37 closings) vs December 2024 (22) = +68% — same direction
metrics.note: 44 homes sold in February 2026 vs 26 in February 2025 — +69% YoY. December 2025 confirms (+68% over Dec 2024). This is a YoY direction indicator, not a recovery % — see the placeholder cards above for the pre-Ian-vs-current comparison once RPCRA data arrives.

sources.source: Redfin Fort Myers Beach housing market data

metrics.label: Median Price + Days on Market — pre-Ian vs current
metrics.note: Current values from Redfin (Feb 2026): median price $580K (−30.7% YoY); 134 days on market (up from 91). The Feb-over-Feb change is direction, not recovery. Pre-Ian (2022) baselines for median price + DOM pending from RPCRA — when received, will show the pre-Ian-vs-current comparison. Median price + DOM are shown here as context indicators (excluded from any recovery %).
metrics.source: Redfin Fort Myers Beach housing market data, February 2026 (current values only); pre-Ian baselines pending RPCRA.

rebuildingActivity.headline: Rebuild surge winding down; recovery funding tapering
rebuildingActivity.framing: Context only — not included in any composite recovery percentage. Permit and disaster-fund activity measures reconstruction surge, not return to normalcy. Both signal sets here are expected to decline as recovery progresses.

rebuildSignals.label: Building Fund Revenue (FY25 → FY26 Budget)
rebuildSignals.note: Permit-fund revenue projected down 29.6% in FY26 — an early signal that the post-Ian rebuilding surge is past peak.
rebuildSignals.source: Town of Fort Myers Beach FY26 Adopted Budget, All Fund Revenues.

rebuildSignals.label: Summer Permit Volume (Jun–Aug YoY)
rebuildSignals.note: Monthly summer permit counts dropped from 109/151/145 (Jun-Aug 2024) to 89/99/101 (Jun-Aug 2025) — a 29% YoY decline in volume that mirrors the Building Fund revenue drop from a different source.
rebuildSignals.source: FMB Chamber of Commerce, Permits sheet (Accommodations file, March 2026).

rebuildSignals.label: Code Enforcement Fees (FY25 → FY26 Budget)
rebuildSignals.note: Code enforcement activity projected down 50% — fewer post-Ian compliance issues as properties return to standard operation.
rebuildSignals.source: Town of Fort Myers Beach FY26 Adopted Budget, Revenues Line Item Detail.

fiscalContext.label: Half-Cent Sales Tax (FY25 → FY26 Budget)
fiscalContext.note: Half-cent sales tax projected down 37% — population displacement and slower commercial activity flowing through to the general fund.
fiscalContext.source: Town of Fort Myers Beach FY26 Adopted Budget.

fiscalContext.label: Emergency Fund / Disaster Reimbursements (FY25 → FY26 Budget)
fiscalContext.note: Federal disaster reimbursements projected down 83% — the recovery-funding tap is closing as Ian's eligible reimbursement window expires.
fiscalContext.source: Town of Fort Myers Beach FY26 Adopted Budget, All Fund Revenues.

fiscalContext.label: FDEM Hurricane Recovery Funds (FY25 → FY26 Budget)
fiscalContext.note: State recovery funds essentially flat at $4.7M — still flowing, but no longer growing. The next budget cycle will likely see this number drop substantially as project-specific allocations close out.
fiscalContext.source: Town of Fort Myers Beach FY26 Adopted Budget, All Fund Revenues.

rules: Compare current value to pre-Ian baseline where available
Cap recovery percentage at 100% (exceeding baseline counts as fully recovered)
Mark 'baseline pending' rather than fabricate when data is unverified
Exclude inverse indicators (e.g., real estate listings — high inventory signals distress)
Surface leading indicators (delinquent VR licenses, café closures) as watchlist, not headline
